title: dense-solver for counting and matching in SAT
description:
A C11 SAT solver by Merlin Numa. Its counting and matching rules recognize when too many requirements compete for too few places. Both rules can be used by other solvers. Version 0.0.4 benchmarks dense-solver against native Kissat and CaDiCaL on 22 public SATLIB formulas and eight SAT Competition 2025 main-track formulas. It includes the 30 inputs, their sources and checksums, raw timings and reproduction commands. The earlier pigeonhole and domino-tiling experiments are also included.

Merlin Numa initiated and directed the Eclipse project, whose v0.0.4 changelog records the original pigeonhole counter on August 19, 2026. Development used the most capable ChatGPT and Claude models available through the author's paid subscriptions at the time. The release includes dated source references and archive fingerprints.
